subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should stale session route state persisted with canonical provider id `openai` be owned by the OpenAI plugin doctor contract, the Codex doctor contract, or a provider-agnostic doctor cleanup path?
rationale: Current source proves the gap, but `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and the Codex app-server route for OpenAI agent turns, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` with tests that clear auto fallback pins only when the configured route no longer allows OpenAI.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI app-server route state
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers intentionally treat OpenAI model-agent session route state as Codex-owned while preserving explicit OpenAI selections.

options.title: Make auto fallback cleanup generic
options.body: Repair stale auto fallback overrides without plugin ownership when the configured route no longer includes the override provider, keeping plugin owners for runtime/auth/CLI-specific state.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` with tests that clear auto fallback pins only when the configured route no longer allows OpenAI.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across the doctor route-state repair, OpenAI identity, Codex migration, and CODEOWNERS signals.
